skill.name: payload
skill.description: Guides Payload CMS development with TypeScript patterns for configuration, collections, fields, hooks, access control, APIs, adapters, queries, and plugins.
skill.summary: Build and troubleshoot Payload CMS applications with practical TypeScript references and security guidance.
skill.author: payloadcms

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, TypeScript examples, local addresses, and standard environment-variable configuration. The IP allowlist example is unsafe because it trusts spoofable forwarding headers and compares CIDR text as a literal value. Semantic review also found empty authentication-secret fallbacks, an access-bypassing preview endpoint, and debugging access functions that always grant permission.

remediation.suggestion: Resolve client addresses through a trusted proxy configuration, reject untrusted forwarding headers, and use a tested CIDR matcher.
Require a non-empty PAYLOAD_SECRET and stop application startup when it is missing or too weak.
Allowlist previewable collections and call the Local API with the requesting user and explicit access enforcement.

remediation.issue: Debug access functions grant all requests
remediation.suggestion: Remove unconditional true returns, delegate to real access rules, and clearly isolate diagnostic logging from production access functions.

semantic_findings.title: Empty Authentication Secret Fallback
semantic_findings.description: Four configuration examples replace a missing PAYLOAD_SECRET with an empty string. If accepted, this creates a predictable secret and risks authentication compromise.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The empty-string fallback is explicit at all four lines. Payload uses this secret for authentication and cryptographic operations.

semantic_findings.title: Preview Endpoint Bypasses Collection Access
semantic_findings.description: The preview endpoint checks only for a user, then performs a dynamic Local API query without access enforcement. Authenticated users may read unauthorized collections.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handler accepts collection and where values from request data and calls req.payload.find without access enforcement. The skill states that Local API access is bypassed by default.

semantic_findings.title: Debug Access Functions Always Grant Permission
semantic_findings.description: Two exported debugging access functions log request metadata and return true unconditionally. Reusing either function as access control grants every request permission.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both examples end with return true after logging and are presented as Access functions. The debugging label reduces production likelihood but not the impact if reused.

content.value_statement: Payload CMS projects combine complex schemas, hooks, queries, and access rules. This skill provides focused TypeScript patterns for building and troubleshooting them.
actual_capabilities: Creates and reviews Payload configuration, collection, field, hook, query, endpoint, and adapter patterns.
Explains secure Local API usage, row-level access control, role checks, and multi-tenant filtering.
Diagnoses transaction, hook recursion, relationship depth, validation, and type-generation problems.
Provides examples for REST, GraphQL, background jobs, storage, email, localization, and plugins.
Uses Payload field guards and TypeScript annotations to preserve safe type narrowing.
References focused documentation for advanced Payload APIs and implementation patterns.
limitations: Examples require adaptation to your Payload version, schema, database, and deployment environment.
The skill does not run migrations, deploy infrastructure, or manage production credentials automatically.
Some reference examples are simplified and require independent security review before production use.
External service integrations require installed adapters, valid accounts, and correctly scoped credentials.

use_cases.title: Model a Content Application
use_cases.description: Create collections, reusable fields, drafts, relationships, hooks, and queries for a new Payload project.

use_cases.title: Review Authorization Rules
use_cases.description: Check Local API calls, role rules, row filters, endpoint authentication, and tenant boundaries for authorization errors.

use_cases.title: Develop a Payload Plugin
use_cases.description: Compose configuration, fields, hooks, components, translations, package exports, and tests without overwriting user settings.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Payload blog collection with drafts, titles, slugs, authors, rich text, and secure default access.

prompt_templates.title: Review Access Control
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Payload access function for authorization gaps and explain how to enforce user permissions with the Local API.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Hook Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this Payload hook failure. Check transaction propagation, recursion controls, operation handling, and returned values.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Tenant Plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-tenant Payload plugin that composes fields, hooks, access rules, filters, translations, and tests without overwriting user configuration.

output_examples.input: Why can a user read posts through my Local API call?
output_examples.output: The review explains the default access bypass, then recommends explicit access enforcement and verification of the requesting user.

output_examples.input: My afterChange hook repeats until the request fails.
output_examples.output: The diagnosis identifies recursive updates and recommends a request-context flag while preserving the original transaction.

output_examples.input: Plan a plugin that adds SEO fields without replacing existing hooks.
output_examples.output: The plan composes existing configuration, respects user overrides, preserves hook arrays, exports types, and defines integration tests.

best_practices: Provide the relevant Payload version, configuration, schema, and failing behavior before requesting changes.
Review generated access rules and endpoints against real roles, tenants, and data sensitivity before deployment.
Run type checks, targeted tests, and migration validation after changing fields, hooks, adapters, or plugins.
anti_patterns: Do not copy simplified authentication, secret, or networking examples directly into production.
Do not assume Local API calls enforce collection access when operating for an authenticated user.
Do not modify generated types manually or run type generation redundantly during active development.

faq.question: Which Payload versions does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers current Payload TypeScript patterns, but every example must be checked against the installed package version.

faq.question: Can it create complete Payload configurations?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft configurations, collections, fields, hooks, access rules, adapters, endpoints, and plugin structures.

faq.question: Does it enforce Local API access automatically?
faq.answer: No. Generated calls must pass the requesting user and explicitly enable access enforcement when acting for that user.

faq.question: Can it diagnose transaction and hook problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks request propagation, nested operations, context flags, operation types, and hook return values.

faq.question: Does it manage database or cloud credentials?
faq.answer: No. Credentials remain your responsibility and should use scoped secret management appropriate for each environment.

faq.question: Can it help develop Payload plugins?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers configuration composition, fields, hooks, admin components, translations, exports, local testing, and end-to-end testing.
